description: `bindaxis <physical axis>` without a virtual axis leaves the axis at GPAD_VIRTAXIS_NONE (-1) and still stores the binding at gaGlobs[0].virtualAxes[-1], which is axesValues[4..5] (the trigger values) instead of rejecting the command.
evidence: reproduced by tests/differential/test_input.py (Axis_Bind_f with two arguments; the original writes the same 8 bytes); reachable from the console and config files

description: A one-character key name returns the char as a signed value, so a byte >= 0x80 gives keynum -128..-1. Key_Bind_f, Key_Unbind_f and Key_SwapBind_f then write keys[keynum].binding up to 1.5 KB before playerKeys (chat field, then gaGlobs, the Axis_*_f_VAR command nodes with their function pointers, cl_input's dvar pointers, playersKb); Key_IsDown/Key_GetBinding read there. `unbind \x80` overwrites the low half of a pointer with 0.
evidence: reproduced by tests/differential/test_input.py (bind/unbind/bind_swap with "\x80", "\xe9", "\xff": the original writes playerKeys-0x4D4 and playerKeys+0x18); reachable from the console and config files; whether a server can make a client run bind/unbind still needs checking (docs/security.md)

description: The mouse is read as the system cursor's movement (GetCursorPos minus the last position, then SetCursorPos back to the window centre), not as raw device counts, so Windows' pointer speed and "Enhance pointer precision" acceleration are applied to aim, and the movement is sampled once per client frame.
evidence: src/win32/win_input.cpp IN_MouseMove reproduces it (tests/differential/test_win_input.py, IN_Frame, 1500 cases); every frame with the game window in front

description: In fullscreen (r_displayMode 0) the cursor is clamped to the window rectangle before the movement is measured, so one frame can't register more than the distance from the centre to the window edge (about 960 counts horizontally at 1920x1080); a fast flick at a low frame rate loses the rest.
evidence: reproduced by tests/differential/test_win_input.py (cursor positions on and beyond the window edges); fullscreen only

description: Every unacknowledged reliable command (up to 128, each up to 1023 characters) is written into a 2048-byte message without checking msg.overflowed. The MSG writers stop at maxsize and set the flag, so the "Overflow compressed msg buf" check never fires and the client sends a truncated packet without its usercmds and end marker.
evidence: tests/differential/test_cl_input_sendcmd.py (message sizes at the 0x800 boundary); reachable by queuing many long reliable commands while the server isn't acknowledging

description: At most 32 usercmds go into a packet; older ones are dropped silently (Black Ops printed MAX_PACKET_USERCMDS).
evidence: reconstruction (count capped at 32); at low packet rates with high frame rates

description: Packets are rate-limited by integer 1000 / cl_maxpackets with cl_maxpackets at most 100, so above 100 fps commands are batched; only loopback is exempt (LAN servers are limited too).
evidence: reconstruction of the inlined CL_ReadyToSendPacket; tests/differential/test_cl_input_sendcmd.py

description: The spawn-sight masks are built with 1 << i for a 16-bit point count into 32-bit masks; points 32 and up (the array holds about 75) shift past the width and set wrong bits.
evidence: reconstruction (tests/differential/test_cl_input_createcmd.py)

description: Remote-control steering with the mouse uses each frame's mouse movement times m_yaw/m_pitch directly as stick deflection (clamped to +-1 per frame), so the same hand movement steers less at higher frame rates.
evidence: reconstruction (tests/differential/test_cl_input_createcmd.py); every remote-controlled vehicle/killstreak with a mouse

description: The location-selection aspect ratio divides by compassMapWorldSize[1]; a zero gives inf/NaN, the clamps let NaN through and it is sent as selectedLoc 0.
evidence: reconstruction; only with bad map compass data
